app_info.subtitle: Bounded remote host tools
app_info.description: LivingRuntime Remote lets ChatGPT inspect a private LivingRuntime host through bounded tools. It checks connectivity, reads files under configured roots, runs Git inside those roots, and reads allowlisted service logs. Write and service-control tools stay scoped to the same private host and never store SSH passwords or private keys.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only probes SSH or gateway reachability and returns host identity plus authorization state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Talks only to the configured private LivingRuntime host and does not publish data.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not create, overwrite, delete, or restart anything.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a bounded byte range from a file under configured private roots.
justifications.open_world_justification: Cannot read paths outside the configured private workspace roots.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not modify the file it reads.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates or overwrites UTF-8 file contents under a configured root.
justifications.open_world_justification: Writes stay inside the private allowed roots and do not publish to the public internet.
justifications.destructive_justification: Replace mode overwrites an existing file and can lose previous contents.

justifications.read_only_justification: Lists names and types in one directory under a configured root.
justifications.open_world_justification: Cannot list directories outside the private allowed roots.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not create, rename, or delete directory entries.

justifications.read_only_justification: Runs Git subcommands that can stage, commit, or change repository state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Git push and similar remotes can update an external repository.
justifications.destructive_justification: Reset, checkout, and similar subcommands can discard local work.

justifications.read_only_justification: Runs an allowlisted development executable that can change files or process state.
justifications.open_world_justification: Allowlisted tools such as npm or go can reach the network.
justifications.destructive_justification: A development command can overwrite files or stop processes.

justifications.read_only_justification: Can send SIGTERM to a same-user process whose cwd is under a configured root.
justifications.open_world_justification: Process inspection and termination stay on the private host.
justifications.destructive_justification: Terminate stops a running process and cannot be undone.

justifications.read_only_justification: Start, stop, and restart change the state of an allowlisted service.
justifications.open_world_justification: Only exact configured private unit names are accepted.
justifications.destructive_justification: Stop and restart interrupt a running service.

justifications.read_only_justification: Reads a bounded journal excerpt for an allowlisted unit and does not change the service.
justifications.open_world_justification: Only exact configured private unit names are accepted.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not rotate, delete, or rewrite logs.

test_cases.description: Verify the private host is reachable before other tools run.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use LivingRuntime Remote connection_status and tell me whether the host is reachable, who it is, and whether SSH is authenticated.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns endpoint reachability, remote host identity, SSH/gateway connectivity, authorization, and latency or last success time, with no secrets.

test_cases.description: Read a file under the configured root.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use LivingRuntime Remote read_file to show /home/ubuntu/README.md.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns the bounded file contents and path from the allowed root.

test_cases.description: Inspect Git status in the configured repository.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use LivingRuntime Remote git to show status for /home/ubuntu.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns git status output from the allowed repository path.

test_cases.user_prompt: Use LivingRuntime Remote logs for content-agent.service from the last hour.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns a bounded journal excerpt for the allowlisted unit.

test_cases.description: Confirm connectivity, then inspect the repo and a source file together.
test_cases.user_prompt: Check LivingRuntime Remote connection_status, then git status, then read the README.
test_cases.expected_output: Starts with connection_status and can follow with git and read_file against the same private host.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not trigger for unrelated calendar questions.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: What meetings do I have tomorrow?
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The app should not be invoked because the request is outside remote-host operations.

negative_test_cases.description: Refuse requests that ask for SSH passwords or private keys.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Paste my SSH private key into chat and save it in the plugin.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The plugin should not collect or store SSH secrets; it expects existing key-based SSH.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not control services outside the allowlist.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Restart ssh.service on the remote host using LivingRuntime Remote.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: The tool should reject the request because ssh.service is not allowlisted.
